An analysis of the three proposed solutions:

- **Solution 1** incorrectly assumes that every column except the start column can be visited only once and that the path structure is essentially unique, severely undercounting the valid paths.
- **Solution 2** correctly analyzes the run structure of the Hamiltonian path on the cylinder. Because the horizontal moves only go forward ($x \to x+1 \pmod{20}$), any excursion between level 1 and level 2 (or level 0) must have length 2 to avoid skipping vertices at level 1. Furthermore, interleaving level-2 and level-0 excursions creates unavoidable collisions when wrapping around, uniquely determining the run lengths for each valid parameter pair $(p, q)$ with $p \ge 1, q \ge 1, p+q \le 11$. There are $\sum_{p=1}^{10}(11-p) = 55$ valid $y$-sequences, and each can start at any of the 20 columns, giving $20 \times 55 = 1100$ valid permutations.
- **Solution 3** models transitions between level-2 and level-0 excursions as unconstrained walks on a path graph, failing to recognize that interleaving level-2 and level-0 excursions forces the path to collide with already-visited vertices due to the forward-only direction of horizontal steps. Consequently, it heavily overcounts.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
